heard: Sunlight bending through Venus's atmosphere creates a glowing halo. We all recognize the moon cycle from crescent to full. Galileo Galilei discovered Venus mimics those same phases in 1610. At full phase, it looks like a tiny distant dot. When closer, it swells into a crescent six times larger. But its most mysterious phase happens against the sun. Astronomers saw a ring of fire during the 1761 transit. Its hidden atmosphere glows before Venus even crosses the sun. That bright ring appears before the disc touches the sun.
